solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Risked opening originally unpopular type of wine

parts.note: a vent is an opening that lets air or gas out

indicators.note: originally points to how a word starts, so only its opening letter is kept

parts.note: first letter of the word
red is a kind of wine

explanation.surface: Someone took a gamble by opening a bottle of an unfashionable wine.
explanation.definitionFit: To venture something is to dare or gamble it, so ventured is a past-tense equivalent of risked.

clue.text: Frenchman turned European Green

indicators.note: something turned faces the other way, so the letters run backwards in this down light

parts.note: E is the standard abbreviation for European
lime is a shade of green

explanation.surface: A Frenchman has switched sides to become a European Green politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Emile is a common French man's first name, so a Frenchman is a fair example-style definition.

clue.text: A rogue with street cred that's hidden from rivals

definitions.note: a descriptive clause standing for the noun: something that's hidden from rivals

indicators.note: a rogue element goes astray and out of order, so the letters beside it are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rascal with urban credibility seems to be someone who keeps things from competitors.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade secret is a business method or formula a firm keeps from its competitors.

clue.text: Supporting soldiers, uplifting praise is excess

definitions.note: residual is used here as a noun, meaning what is left over

indicators.note: in a down light, supporting means sitting underneath, so the following material goes below the soldiers

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

indicators.note: lifting up in a down light makes the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: laud means praise, followed by is as written

explanation.surface: Backing the troops with too much flattering praise is overdoing it.
explanation.definitionFit: A residual is a remainder or surplus amount left over, so it can stand for an excess.

clue.text: Curse those goats all over teenagers' stuff?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: read literally, a cry of 'Down with!' aimed at young goats, kids
second meaning: the idiom for being in touch with youth culture

explanation.walkthrough: Kids are young goats, and 'down with X!' is a curse; the question mark flags the playful literal reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone down with the kids is keen on and familiar with whatever young people like, idiomatically all over it.

clue.text: Very much noble fellow making entry in empty diary

indicators.note: making an entry means going inside, so the fellow sits within the other letters
an emptied word loses its contents, leaving only the outside letters

parts.note: first and last letters
an earl is a nobleman

explanation.surface: An aristocrat squeezes himself into a blank page of a diary.
explanation.definitionFit: Dearly is an adverb of intensity, as in 'I would dearly love to', meaning greatly.

clue.text: Manage shots I had returned on court

definitions.note: to manage the shots is what a film director does

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so these two letters run backwards

parts.note: contraction of I had
re means on or about
CT is an abbreviation of court

explanation.surface: A tennis player reports which shots were sent back over the net.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites tennis, but the shots belong to a film set.
explanation.definitionFit: A film director manages how each shot is taken, so to direct is to manage shots.

clue.text: Dust and clean, losing weight

indicators.note: losing something means it is dropped, so a letter comes out of the word

parts.note: to wash is to clean
W is the abbreviation for weight

explanation.surface: A housekeeping chore list: dust and wash things, while slimming down.
explanation.definitionFit: Ash is the fine powdery residue left after burning, a kind of dust.

clue.text: Put garland on certainly in casual manner

definitions.note: leisurely works as an adverb here, meaning in an unhurried way

indicators.note: in a down light, on means placed above, so the garland comes first

parts.note: a lei is a Hawaiian flower garland
surely means certainly

explanation.surface: An instruction to hang flowers on someone, delivered in a relaxed way.
explanation.definitionFit: Leisurely, as an adverb, describes acting without hurry, which is a relaxed, unhurried manner.

clue.text: Recalled exactly what one needs and beats high-achievers

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word runs in the backward direction

parts.note: 'that's it!' means that's exactly what is wanted
to tan someone is to beat them

explanation.surface: Remembering precisely what someone needs, and outdoing it, marks out the top performers.
explanation.definitionFit: Titans are giants of their field, people of outstanding power or success.

clue.text: One with rough coat, superior clothing according to Spooner

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts are exchanged

parts.note: higher means superior and wear means clothing; swapping their opening sounds

explanation.surface: A dog's shaggy coat is described as top-quality attire.
explanation.definitionFit: A wirehair is a dog breed, such as the wirehaired terrier, with a rough, wiry coat.

clue.text: Announced future outdoor event

indicators.note: something announced is spoken out, so we go by how the word sounds

parts.note: fate is what the future holds

explanation.surface: Plans for an open-air event coming up have been made public.
explanation.definitionFit: A fete is an outdoor fair or garden party, often held to raise money for a cause.

clue.text: Shun a crowd merrily singing in the morning

indicators.note: doing something merrily means in a carefree, jumbled way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone avoids the throng, cheerfully singing early in the day.
explanation.definitionFit: The dawn chorus is the sound of many birds singing together at daybreak.

clue.text: Missing no more, chess piece found under toilet

indicators.note: in a down light, under means placed below, so the chess piece follows the toilet

parts.note: over means finished, no more
loo is British slang for a toilet
the king is a chess piece

explanation.surface: Someone is no longer missing a lost chess piece, found beneath the toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Overlooking something means failing to notice it, so it is being missed.

clue.text: Painting back of article with certainty it's man-made object

parts.note: painting is a form of art

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final position, so only its last letter is used

parts.note: last letter of the word
a fact is something known with certainty

explanation.surface: A painting which, the article confidently states, is a human creation.
explanation.definitionFit: An artefact is any object made by people, especially one of historical interest.

clue.text: Speak for a revolutionary with grudge

indicators.note: a revolution turns things round, so the word for a is read backwards

parts.note: per means a, as in five pounds a head
to grudge is to resent

explanation.surface: Someone acts as spokesman for a rebel who bears a grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: To represent someone is to act or speak on their behalf, as an agent or MP does.

clue.text: Bounteous land herd means to use regularly

indicators.note: using something regularly means at fixed intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A fertile region where a herd's resources are meant for routine use.
explanation.definitionFit: Eden is the biblical garden of plenty, used for any place of abundance and delight.

clue.text: Learner of climbing, junior devotee

indicators.note: climbing goes upwards, which in a down light reads the letters from bottom to top

parts.note: L is the learner-driver symbol, then of as written
junior means lower in rank

explanation.surface: A novice mountaineer is a keen but junior fan of the sport.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower is a supporter or adherent of a person or cause, which is what a devotee is.

clue.text: Pole pointed weapon heartlessly

indicators.note: without its heart a word loses its central letter

parts.note: a spear is a pointed weapon

explanation.surface: A Polish soldier cruelly pointed a weapon at someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a person from Poland; here it is a long piece of timber.
explanation.definitionFit: A spar is a stout pole, such as a mast or boom on a ship.

clue.text: People out to offend nurses electrify unoccupied patient beds, say

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so the first word wraps around the next letters

parts.note: trolls post online to provoke and offend

indicators.note: an unoccupied word has had its inside emptied, leaving only its outside letters

parts.note: first and last letters

explanation.surface: Online provocateurs care for patients by wiring up empty hospital beds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nurses' sounds like hospital staff; it is the verb meaning to hold.
explanation.definitionFit: Hospital trolleys are wheeled stretchers, an example of beds for patients, hence the 'say'.

clue.text: Starts demoting good people

indicators.note: demoting a letter for good moves it lower, rearranging the word's order

parts.note: begins means starts

explanation.surface: A company begins demoting its good staff.
explanation.walkthrough: G stands for good; demoting it in this down light shifts it two places lower in the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Beings are living creatures, and human beings are people.

clue.text: Kitchen appliance inventor handled gym equipment

parts.note: a kettle is a kitchen appliance
Alexander Graham Bell, inventor of the telephone

explanation.surface: An inventor dealt with a piece of kitchen kit and exercise apparatus.
explanation.definitionFit: A kettlebell is an iron weight with a handle on top, used for exercise.

clue.text: Sack son carried in public

indicators.note: something carried in is held within, so the letter goes inside the other word

parts.note: out means known publicly
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A boy is lugged along in a bag for all to see.
explanation.definitionFit: To sack someone is to dismiss them, which is to remove or oust them.

clue.text: Metal appropriate in auditorium

indicators.note: an auditorium is where an audience listens, so the word is taken by sound

parts.note: to appropriate is to take without permission

explanation.surface: Metal fittings that suit a concert hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' reads as the adjective meaning suitable; here it is the verb to take.
explanation.definitionFit: Steel is an alloy of iron and carbon, commonly called a metal.

clue.text: That man left winter sports equipment outside in Nordic city

indicators.note: outside means surrounding, so the equipment wraps around the next word

parts.note: he refers to that man
L is the abbreviation for left
a ski is winter sports gear
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man abandoned his skis outdoors in a Scandinavian town.
explanation.definitionFit: Helsinki is the capital of Finland, a Nordic country.

clue.text: Look for missing king and judge

indicators.note: something missing has gone, so that letter is taken out of the word

parts.note: to seek is to look for
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A search is on for a lost monarch and a magistrate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look' tempts as the definition, but 'Look for' is one phrase in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To see something a certain way is to judge or regard it, as in 'as I see it'.

clue.text: Wife distressed lamented

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for wife
to ail is to trouble or distress

explanation.surface: A wife, upset, mourned aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Wailing is crying out in grief, so wailed is a past-tense equivalent of lamented.

clue.text: Books the property of that lady, not me

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a set of books
hers means belonging to her

explanation.surface: Those books belong to her, she insists, not to me.
explanation.definitionFit: Others means other people, everyone apart from oneself, so it stands for those who are not me.

clue.text: Try hard setting floor covering on stone with diminished joy

indicators.note: diminished means made smaller, so the word loses its final letter
setting one thing on another places them in sequence, here after the stone

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, a British unit of weight
a rug covers a floor
glee means joy

explanation.surface: Laying a carpet on a stone floor is hard work that saps one's cheer.
explanation.definitionFit: To struggle is to make a great effort against difficulty, which is trying hard.
